questions.question: State the limitations associated with Mobile Journalism. / [CO1]
questions.solution_html:
• State the limitations associated with Mobile Journalism.
  • Ans: Mobile Journalism (MoJo) has several limitations despite its convenience. It faces
  • technical constraints such as limited battery life, storage, and lower production quality
  • compared to professional equipment. There are issues with audio and video quality,
  • especially in noisy or low-light environments. Journalists may lack advanced editing tools on
  • mobile devices. It also raises concerns about credibility and verification, as quick reporting
  • may lead to errors. Additionally, MoJo journalists often face safety risks, network
  • dependency, and lack of institutional support, which can affect the depth and reliability of
  • reporting.

questions.question: Classify different types of biases that influence digital media consumption. / [CO3]
questions.solution_html:
• Classify different types of biases that influence digital media consumption.
  • Ans: Digital media consumption is influenced by various biases. Confirmation bias leads
  • users to prefer information that supports their existing beliefs. Algorithmic bias occurs when
  • platforms show content based on past behaviour. Selection bias limits exposure to diverse
  • viewpoints. Cultural and social bias shape interpretation based on background. Framing bias
  • influences how information is presented, and availability bias makes people rely on easily
  • accessible information. These biases create echo chambers and filter bubbles, restricting
  • balanced understanding.

questions.question: Outline the objectives and focus areas of the Digital India Programme. / [CO1]
questions.solution_html:
• Outline the objectives and focus areas of the Digital India Programme.
  • Ans: The Digital India Programme aims to transform India into a digitally empowered
  • society and knowledge economy. Its objectives include providing digital infrastructure as a
  • core utility, ensuring governance and services on demand, and promoting digital literacy. Key
  • focus areas are broadband connectivity, e-governance, digital payments, cybersecurity, and
  • skill development. It also encourages innovation, startup culture, and inclusion of rural
  • populations in the digital ecosystem.

questions.question: Describe how algorithmic amplification supports the spread of manipulated content. / [CO2]
questions.solution_html:
• Describe how algorithmic amplification supports the spread of manipulated content.
  • Ans: Algorithmic amplification refers to how digital platforms promote content based on
  • engagement metrics such as likes, shares, and comments. Manipulated content often spreads
  • quickly because it is sensational, emotional, or controversial, attracting more interaction.
  • Algorithms prioritise such content, increasing its visibility and reach. This leads to the rapid
  • spread of misinformation, fake news, and propaganda, often without proper verification. As a
  • result, users are exposed to biased or misleading information, reinforcing echo chambers and
  • polarisation.

questions.question: Outline the major platforms used in online news dissemination. / [CO1]
questions.solution_html:
• Outline the major platforms used in online news dissemination.
  • Ans: Online news is disseminated through multiple platforms, including news websites and
  • portals, social media platforms (Facebook, X, Instagram), mobile news apps, blogs and
  • independent journalism sites, and video platforms like YouTube. Messaging apps such as
  • WhatsApp and Telegram also play a major role in news sharing. These platforms enable
  • instant, wide, and interactive distribution of news content.

questions.question: Identify the technical competencies necessary in online journalism. / [CO1]
questions.solution_html:
• Identify the technical competencies necessary in online journalism.
  • Ans: Online journalists require several technical skills, including digital writing and editing,
  • multimedia production (audio, video, graphics), and basic photography and videography.
  • They must be skilled in content management systems (CMS), social media handling, and
  • SEO (Search Engine Optimization). Knowledge of data journalism, fact-checking tools, and
  • analytics is also essential. Additionally, they need adaptability to new technologies and
  • digital tools.

questions.question: Summarize the steps involved in verifying a viral photograph. / [CO4]
questions.solution_html:
• Summarize the steps involved in verifying a viral photograph.
  • Ans: Verifying a viral photograph involves several steps. First, conduct a reverse image
  • search to find the original source. Check the metadata for details like date and location.
  • Analyse the image for visual inconsistencies or manipulation. Verify the context by cross-
  • checking with reliable news sources. Use geolocation tools to confirm the location. Finally,
  • consult fact-checking websites to ensure authenticity before sharing.

questions.question: Describe common techniques used to manipulate textual information. / [CO4] [5x5 = 25]
questions.solution_html:
• Describe common techniques used to manipulate textual information.
  • Ans: Textual information can be manipulated in various ways. Selective editing or omission
  • can distort meaning. Misleading headlines (clickbait) attract attention but misrepresent
  • content. Use of emotional or loaded language influences reader perception. False attribution
  • or fake quotes create misinformation. Context manipulation presents information out of
  • context, and fabrication of facts or statistics misleads audiences. These techniques are often
  • used to influence opinions and spread propaganda.

questions.question: Identify the structural and technical elements involved in web content creation and editing. / [CO1]
questions.solution_html:
• Identify the structural and technical elements involved in web content creation and
  • editing.
  • Ans: Web content creation and editing involve both structural and technical elements.
  • Structurally, content must have a clear headline, subheadings, introduction, body, and
  • conclusion for readability. It should follow logical flow, coherence, and proper formatting
  • such as bullet points and short paragraphs. Technically, it requires knowledge of Content
  • Management Systems (CMS), HTML basics, and Search Engine Optimization (SEO)
  • techniques like keyword usage and meta descriptions. Other elements include multimedia
  • integration (images, videos, infographics), hyperlinking, and mobile responsiveness. Editing
  • involves proofreading, fact-checking, grammar correction, and plagiarism checking to ensure
  • accuracy, clarity, and credibility.

questions.question: Explain the stages involved in debunking fake news systematically. / [CO3]
questions.solution_html:
• Explain the stages involved in debunking fake news systematically.
  • Ans: Debunking fake news involves a systematic process. First is identification, where
  • suspicious content is recognized. Next is verification, using tools like reverse image search,
  • metadata analysis, and source checking. The third stage is cross-checking, where information
  • is compared with credible news sources and fact-checking websites. Then comes analysis,
  • identifying bias, manipulation, or misleading context. After that, evidence collection is done
  • to support the correction. Finally, correction and dissemination involve clearly presenting the
  • verified facts to the public to counter misinformation. This process ensures accuracy,
  • transparency, and public awareness.

questions.question: Reproduce the performance features of traditional media. / [CO1] [15x1 = 15]
questions.solution_html:
• Reproduce the performance features of traditional media.
  • Ans: Traditional media such as newspapers, radio, and television have distinct performance
  • features. They are considered highly credible and authoritative, especially in news
  • dissemination. They follow structured and professional editorial processes, ensuring accuracy
  • and reliability. Traditional media provide wide reach and mass audience coverage,
  • particularly in regional and rural areas. They maintain fixed schedules and formats, offering
  • consistency and discipline in content delivery. Additionally, they support cultural
  • preservation, public awareness, and educational functions. However, they are generally one-
  • way communication systems, with limited audience interaction compared to digital media.
